items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: And I think everyone knows that it was Mitch Miller. And Mitch Miller just made one comment on hearing the tape, that he didn't find it exciting.

ctx.x: Oh, I see. How did that come down? He asked you to front it?

Well, he had been a press agent for me many years and many years ago, and actually, when we came back from the '54 tour in Europe, with that band, Bill Perkins and people like that, Nat was on that tour and on that trip Johnny Howell and people -- Howie, this friend of mine, heard the band, and we'd had a successful European tour. And he said, 'Boy, this band should make some records right now, it's really ripe.' And I said, 'Fine.'

So he got everybody -- somebody, I should say, at Columbia steamed up, and we went over and made a session. And we were all pleased with it. And -- but a strange thing had happened at Columbia. There was now a new head of the pop and jazz and everything department. And I think everyone knows that it was Mitch Miller.
